params.body:
## Why

The garage table on Beheer > Inzichten > Activiteit stood every measure in one row of equal columns, sorted on "Handelingen". It read as "what this garage did", but four of the columns count what somebody else did with the garage's cars. A garage with a busy website looked active while nobody there had signed in, and the reverse.

## What changes

- `Measures::GROUPS` puts every measure in one of two groups, in the catalogue itself: `own` (what the garage's own people do on the platform) and `reach` (what others do with its cars). `Measures::ALL` is those groups one after the other, own first; `Measures::group()` answers for one measure.
- The garage table has a row of group heads above the column heads ("Wat de garage doet", "Bereik van haar wagens"), room and one quiet rule between the groups, and its own frame to scroll in. Sorting is still per column and the default sort is still handlings.
- The measure table, which is the picker on this screen (click a row), lists the measures under the same two heads.
- Under the chart title a sentence says whose action the number is. For a reach measure it names the colleague or the visitor.
- "Handelingen" keeps its name; a line under the garage table says what it holds.
- Labels that read as the garage acting are reworded in nl, fr, en and de ("Wagens in de websitewidget" is now "Wagens bekeken in de websitewidget", "Widget geopend" is "Widget geopend door bezoekers", "Weergaven" is "Schermen geopend", and the no-hours line no longer says "Weergaven" for every daily measure).
- Two new measures in the own group, for how much a garage itself looks in the shared stocklist (below).
- A measure that was never counted is no longer compared with "0 before": it has no period before it. The "since" cell then says "nog niet geteld".

Nothing that was counted or stored before is counted or stored differently.

## Who is the actor of each measure

| Measure | Counted row | Actor | Garage on the row | Group |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Handelingen | eight sources, `Activity::SOURCES` | mixed, see below | see below | own |
| Bewerkingen | `activity_events`, kind `vehicle.edited` | a signed-in person saving a car (jobs and commands write nothing) | the user's garage | own |
| Schermen geopend | `activity_page_views`, all routes | a signed-in person loading a whole page | the user's garage | own |
| Stocklist geopend (new) | `activity_page_views`, route `stocklist.index.showExtendedSearch` | a signed-in person loading the stocklist list | the user's garage | own |
| Wagens bekeken in de stocklist (new) | `vehicle_lookups` | a signed-in person opening a colleague's car | the viewer's garage | own |
| Aanmeldingen | `activity_events`, kind `user.signed_in` | a person signing in | the user's garage | own |
| Wagens bekeken door collega's | `vehicle_views`, source `platform` | a signed-in user of another garage (the owner's own opens go to `own` and are in no measure) | the owner of the car | reach |
| Wagens bekeken in de websitewidget | `vehicle_views`, source `embed` | an anonymous visitor of the garage's website widget | the owner of the car | reach |
| Wagens bekeken op de eigen website | `vehicle_views`, source `site` | an anonymous visitor of the garage's website on the public API | the owner of the car | reach |
| Widget geopend door bezoekers | `embed_views` | an anonymous visitor opening the widget | the garage of the widget | reach |

**Handelingen is the one mixed measure.** It is the union of eight sources: cars entered (`vehicles.created_at`, on the garage of the car, so a car that arrives through an import feed counts too), offers and order forms (garage of the user who made them), bids (`export_bids` where the bidder is a dealer), Car-Pass, VIN and AutoConnect lookups (garage of the user), and leads (`leads`, on the garage that received it). A lead is written by a customer, so that part is not the garage acting. Edits and photos are not in it. It stays in the own group because seven of the eight sources are, and the screen now says what it holds. Splitting leads out would change what is counted, which this pull request does not do.

## The garage's own looking: what was stored, and what one unit is

**Cars viewed in the stocklist.** `vehicle_views` keeps the owner of the car only. The viewer's garage was known inside the insert (it decides `own` against `platform`) and then dropped, so the question could not be answered from what was stored. This adds `vehicle_lookups` (day, viewing garage, car, count), written in the same call for a platform view by a signed-in user whose garage does not own the car. One unit is one open of a colleague's car detail; one row per day, garage and car, so views and distinct cars can both be read (the screen shows views). It starts on the first day after the deploy; before that the measure says it was not counted and is not compared. Nothing is derived backwards. The page counter was not used as a stand-in: it cannot leave out a garage's own cars and it skips a detail loaded in a modal, so it would have been a third number disagreeing with its own mirror.

**Stocklist opened.** Already stored: `activity_page_views` keeps a daily total per person per route since 26 September 2026, with the user's garage on the row. The measure is that counter narrowed to the list itself (`GET /stocklist`). One unit is one whole page load by a signed-in person, summed over the per-person daily totals; filtering and scrolling on inside the list are not page loads and do not count. It is a part of "Schermen geopend", not a number beside it.

**Staff.** No measure on this screen sets staff apart, and these two do not either: a user counts under the garage on his account. A user without a garage is in the totals of the page counter and in no garage row; for cars viewed in the stocklist he writes no row (his view still counts for the owner of the car).

## Business rules

R P3-16.24 (the two groups, the heads, what a handling is) and R P3-16.25 (the garage's own looking) are new; R P3-16.13 points to the groups.

## Tests

`WhatAGarageDoesIsNotWhatOthersDoWithItsCarsTest` (10 tests, `@rule P3-16.24` and `P3-16.25`): every measure has exactly one group and the own group comes first; the garage table carries both group heads with the right span and the columns under the right group; the picker lists the measures per group; the sentence of every reach measure names the outsider in four languages; the handlings note is on the page; every group, measure and sentence exists in nl, fr, en and de; a car opened in the stocklist counts for the garage that looked and not when it is its own; the measure is dated from its first day and keeps no person; stocklist opened is the page counter of that one screen.

Run locally: the Activity, Measures and insights test classes, `Rules*Test`, `LanguageParityTest`, `QualityRatchetTest`, `StylesheetSyntaxTest`, `TheThemeOverrulesEverySpacingClassTest` (194 tests, green), PHPStan (no errors), Pint on the new files, `npm run build`. The full suite was not run locally because other suites were running on the same machine; CI is the judge.

No screenshots: the machine was too loaded to start a server with demo data.

## Deploy

One migration (`vehicle_lookups`), run by the deploy. The screen's cache key moves to `activity.screen.6`.
params.title: Activity separates what a garage does from the reach of its cars
